title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The previous page studies a functor f: C' -> C between groupoids (in context, pieces of Teichmüller-type groupoids) with an action of a group mu on C'. The conditions are: (b) f is mu-equivariant, with mu acting trivially on C. (c) mu acts freely on Ob C', and Ob C'/mu -> Ob C is bijective. (d) Each fibre C'_y is a connected 'Pi-groupoid' with mu acting on it.

The page 93 computation. Phi is a connected Pi-groupoid, meaning its Hom sets are Pi-torsors (Pi is effectively abelian, or one works with bitorsors). mu acts on Phi, and Ob Phi = E is a mu-torsor. Write H_{x,y} = Hom_Phi(x,y). The action of alpha in mu gives isomorphisms H_{x,y} -> H_{alpha x, alpha y}. These form a transitive system of identifications among the H_{x,y} with fixed 'difference' u = y^{-1}x in mu. Identifying along this system gives Pi-torsors H_u, one for each u in mu. Composition then gives associative isomorphisms H_u ∧ H_v ≅ H_{uv}.

This page.
(1) The data above is exactly what is needed to define a group extension 1 -> Pi -> E_Phi -> mu -> 1, with E_Phi = ⊔_u H_u. Equivalently, E_Phi is the vertex group of the action groupoid Phi//mu: pairs (alpha, phi: x -> alpha x). The parenthetical NB says the commutativity of mu has not been used.
(2) Conversely, an extension 1 -> Pi -> E -> mu -> 1 is the same as a Pi-torsor E over mu with a multiplicative structure. From it one builds canonically a connected Pi-groupoid Phi(E): objects form a mu-torsor (e.g. E/Pi), and Hom(x,y) is the fibre of E over y x^{-1}. mu acts on Phi(E) by transport of structure (translation).
(3) Conclusion (17): an equivalence of categories between
  - connected Pi-groupoids Phi with a mu-action on (Phi, Pi) such that Ob Phi is a mu-torsor, and
  - extensions of mu by Pi.
(4) Fixing one extension E once and for all, Grothendieck defines an 'E(Pi,mu)-structure' on C' over C. On top of (a)-(c), each fibre over an object of C is given a Phi-structure, i.e. an identification of its associated extension with E. The next page discusses the compatibility of these identifications along connected components. It also gives a model case: coverings deduced from a U-torsor P/T with mu ⊂ U normal, U_0 = U/mu, and E/Pi ≅ pi_1(U_0).

Purpose. To axiomatize when a 'mu-covering' C' -> C of (Teichmüller) groupoids carries a coherent central or abelian-kernel extension structure, as a fibrewise version of the extension 1 -> Pi -> E -> mu -> 1. This is presumably aimed at the extensions of Teichmüller groupoids arising from torsors (roots of unity, determinant- or Picard-type torsors) over moduli spaces.

The marginal note (only partly legible) says that under the hypotheses made, the extension acquires a canonical splitting; the details are illegible.
errors: No mathematical error. Forming H_u ∧ H_v needs Pi abelian (or the fibres must be treated as bitorsors); the marginal remark about the commutativity of Pi seems to acknowledge this.
The equivalence (17) is stated without checking functoriality on morphisms, but it is standard and correct.
'C au-dessus de C' must be 'C' au-dessus de C'.

ideas.what: Equivalence between connected groupoids with a free and transitive mu-action on objects (Hom sets being Pi-torsors) and extensions of mu by Pi, via the vertex group of the action groupoid.
ideas.modern_name: Action groupoid / Grothendieck construction: groupoids with free transitive group action on objects vs. group extensions; Pi-banded gerbe over the point with mu-equivariance
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; Grothendieck (SGA1 descent), Giraud (non-abelian cohomology, liens), R. Brown (groupoid treatments)
ideas.where_published: Closely related formalism in SGA1 and in Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne; not this exact statement as far as known

ideas.what: Group extension of mu by Pi described as Pi-torsors H_u over mu with associative isomorphisms H_u ∧ H_v ≅ H_{uv}.
ideas.modern_name: Extensions as multiplicative torsors (torsor with group-law structure)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, SGA7 Exposé VII (extensions and biextensions)

ideas.what: Notion of an 'E(Pi,mu)-structure' on a mu-covering C' -> C of groupoids: fibrewise Pi-groupoids identified with a fixed extension.
ideas.modern_name: Fibred groupoid extension; equivariant gerbe / central extension of a groupoid along a covering
ideas.usually_credited_to: General theory of gerbes and groupoid extensions (Giraud; later Breen, Moerdijk and others)

missed.claim: A formalism, intended for Teichmüller groupoids, of coverings carrying a fixed extension structure E(Pi,mu), modelled on torsors under U with mu ⊂ U and pi_1(U/mu). It apparently aims at a canonical treatment of extensions of the Teichmüller tower by roots-of-unity or torus-torsors. The general algebra is routine; the intended application is not developed on this page.
missed.quote: on dit qu'on a une E(Π,μ) structure sur C' au-dessus de C
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Possibly relevant to central extensions of mapping class groupoids (determinant line, level/spin structures) acted on by Gal(Q̄/Q). It is only a setup here, and its value depends on later pages.

deep.surprise_reason: The page records a standard equivalence between groupoids with a free mu-action and group extensions, in the style of Grothendieck's own SGA7 torsor description of extensions. It is new only as a preparatory step toward extension structures on Teichmüller groupoids.
transcription_corrections: The first exact sequence should begin '1 → Π → E_Φ → μ → 1'. The underbrace under E_Φ reads 'Φ ↦ sa (Π,μ) structure' (approximately).
'CAB' is probably '(NB' or '(NB on n'a pas utilisé la commutativité de μ encore)'.
'(par voie commutative)' is likely '(pour μ commutatif)' or similar.
'implique la donnée d'un torseur E sur μ' is more likely 'i.e. la donnée d'un torseur E sur μ' (E → μ seen as a Π-torsor over μ).
'Φ = E(E)' is likely 'Φ = Φ(E)', the groupoid constructed from the extension E.
'sur C au-dessus de C' should be 'sur C' au-dessus de C'.
'pour toute f ∈ Ob G' is likely 'pour tout ξ (or y) ∈ Ob C'.
